THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Marathon County supervisors punted a Hub City Wind resolution back to committee while adopting new rules on battery storage and data centers; Wausau's finance committee meanwhile advanced a tax increment bond for a downtown development and wrestled with lead-service-line funding gaps.

  • Marathon County adopted a temporary moratorium on data centers and a battery energy storage ordinance requiring 500-foot setbacks from all structures, then referred an unresolved Hub City Wind resolution back to the Executive Committee for a clearer recommendation at September's meeting.
  • The Wausau Finance Committee approved a tax increment revenue bond for the Foundry on Third development and adopted a four-session budget workshop calendar beginning October 5 at 6:30 p.m.
  • The Village of Weston approved a $1.29 million waterworks revenue bond and voted to hold trustee pay flat for the 2027–2029 term at $7,200 for trustees and $8,400 for the village president.
  • The Wausau Police & Fire Commission launched a deputy chief promotional process — applications open in September, with a decision expected at the December meeting — framed as early police-chief succession planning.
  • Weston's Parks Committee gave Everest Youth Hockey the green light to develop a feasibility plan for a 30,000-square-foot indoor community space at Kennedy Park, with no village funds committed.
  • Kronenwetter's Village Board is set to vote on accepting the Village Clerk's resignation at a special meeting called for August 27.

Coming up: The Wausau Committee of the Whole meets Wednesday, September 2 at 5:30 p.m. — worth watching given the budget and development threads active at the Finance Committee — and the City's Economic Development Committee convenes Tuesday, September 1 at 5:30 p.m.
